### Issue description

Empty `period` results are inconsistent

The code below outputs

### Reproducible example

```python
df = pl.DataFrame({'ts': [datetime(2020, 1, 1)], 'values': [1]}).sort('ts')
print(df.select(pl.col('values').rolling_sum(by='ts', window_size='0d', closed='left')))
print(df.select(pl.col('values').rolling_sum(by='ts', window_size='0d', closed='right')))
print(df.select(pl.col('values').rolling_sum(by='ts', window_size='0d', closed='both')))
print(df.select(pl.col('values').rolling_sum(by='ts', window_size='0d', closed='none')))
```


### Expected behavior

The window here, in the different cases, is:
- [2020-01-01, 2020-01-01)
- (2020-01-01, 2020-01-01]
- [2020-01-01, 2020-01-01]
- (2020-01-01, 2020-01-01)

review_comments: So all this didn't hit any test? Just to be sure, windows may still be lagging right?

There are three branches here:

- if period > 0
- if period == 0 and closed is right or both
- if period == 0 and closed is left or none

if `period == 0` is disallowed, then only the first one is necessary, and the `if` statement can be removed and the code detended

`offset` and `period` are the same here, they just differ in sign, because the `rolling_*` functions don't have an `offset` argument. Windows where `offset != period` (like, that for point `2022-01-05` the window is `[2022-01-03, 2022-01-04)`) are only possible for `groupby_rolling` (and that's unaffected by this PR)
Thanks for explanation. Sorry for the questions on my side. I am working on many things, so I try to get an understanding without getting fully in the code. Looks good!

Thanks! And please always do ask for clarifications when things aren't clear, this'll also help anyone in the future who ends up here from a `git blame` trying to figure out why a certain change was made
